forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough transport spending is £7.7m so far, against a £10.2m year-to-date budget
news_drafts.lead:
Day-to-day spending on transport at the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough combined authority stands at £7.7m for the year to date, against a year-to-date budget of £10.2m, an underspend of £2.5m. The figures are in the Budget and Performance Report going to the Transport Committee on 4 November.

The report says most of the year-to-date underspend sits in public transport bus services. In its words, "the underspend here is because of a lag in billing from contractors". The report does not present the year-to-date gap as a saving for the year.

The full-year budget for transport is £23.8m and the full-year forecast is £23.7m, a variance of £125k below budget. The report gives a separate reason for that forecast variance: the start of the Market Towns Cycle Support scheme has been delayed and its spending is now spread over three years.

findings.headline: Transport income of £39m received to date in 2026/27, with the full-year forecast in line with the £86,531k budget
findings.detail: The paper reports that income to date is in line with expectations and that the forecast outturn matches the expected budget. The Transport Levy income line is £1,079k ahead of its year-to-date budget.
findings.matters: Income forecast on budget at the half-year point, with a levy line running ahead of profile, is a position finance officers at peer councils would compare with their own mid-year income tracking.
findings.figures: Total transport income FY budget £86,531k; FY forecast £86,531k; FY variance £0k; YTD actual £38,873k against YTD budget £37,791k; income to date £39m
findings.quote: The income received to date in the year is £39m in line with expectations.

findings.headline: Transport revenue expenditure at £7,702k year to date against a £10,221k budget, with the underspend attributed to a lag in contractor billing
findings.detail: The paper says most of the year-to-date underspend sits in public transport bus services because contractors' billing is lagging. The full-year forecast shows a £125k variance, from the Market Towns Cycle Support start being delayed and spread over three years.
findings.matters: Billing lags make year-to-date underspends look larger than the eventual outturn, which finance directors reviewing mid-year monitoring figures would need to allow for.
findings.figures: YTD actual £7,702k against YTD budget £10,221k; YTD variance -£2,519k; FY budget £23,831k; FY forecast £23,706k; FY variance -£125k
findings.quote: the underspend here is because of a lag in billing from contractors

findings.headline: Road Safety Fund capital forecast at £150k against a £590k budget, with the variance attributed to delays in agreeing the Grant Funding Agreement
findings.detail: The paper says the variance reflects timing changes and rescheduled resource, following delays in agreeing the grant funding legal document. A revised agreement is now being agreed. Year-to-date spend is nil against a £120k budget.
findings.matters: Grant-funded programmes whose spend depends on a legal agreement being finalised are exposed to the same delay, and finance teams elsewhere would want to see how long that step takes.
findings.figures: FY budget £590k; FY forecast £150k; FY variance -£440k; deferral £440k; YTD budget £120k
findings.quote: delays in agreeing the Grant Funding Agreement (GFA) legal document

findings.headline: March junction improvements forecast at £4,914k against a £5,321k budget, with a two-year extension to 2028/29 sought to fund Hostmoor Avenue
findings.detail: The paper attributes the underspend to efficiencies and a revised traffic-management approach on the A141 / Twenty Foot Road works, and to NILR detailed design not progressing. Approval is being sought to use the underspend for Hostmoor Avenue and to extend the funding and delivery period, with no intended increase in CPCA funding.
findings.matters: Re-using an underspend on a funded scheme and extending its delivery period, without new CPCA money, is a reprofiling decision that finance officers managing similar programme underspends would want to compare with their own approval routes.
findings.figures: FY budget £5,321k; FY forecast £4,914k; FY variance -£407k; YTD actual £1,882k against YTD budget £2,406k; extension from 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.quote: to extend the funding/delivery period by two financial years from 2026/27 to 2028/29

findings.headline: A141 capital forecast at £1,800k against a £2,275k budget, with the variance attributed to refreshing the Outline Business Case for the High Growth scenario
findings.detail: The paper says the A141 and St Ives programme is being re-examined so the package responds to the High Growth scenario. The period will also cover consultation outcomes, surveys and technical work ahead of Preliminary Designs and the Full Business Case.
findings.matters: A scheme moving back to business case refresh before design work continues is a timing change that finance officers managing pre-construction spend on growth-linked schemes would want to see in their own profiles.
findings.figures: FY budget £2,275k; FY forecast £1,800k; FY variance -£475k; deferral £475k; YTD actual £453k
findings.quote: the Outline Business Case to consider how the package should evolve to respond to the High Growth scenario
